TechCrunch reports that investment bank Jefferies estimated those restrictions could reduce Nvidia’s data-centre revenue by $44bn to $62bn next year; Kress said strong demand for other products meant the rules would not affect the company’s top-line revenue. The longer-term effect on Nvidia’s customers and competitors remains uncertain.

content.headline: US senators seek AI security plan after wave of technology outages
content.shortHeadline: Senators press US AI chief on cyber vulnerabilities
content.standfirst: A bipartisan pair of senators says AI can expose software weaknesses faster than organisations can patch them and wants the White House AI chief to strengthen critical infrastructure. Officials say the recent outages are not known to be linked or caused by an attack.

image.caption: Jay Clayton arrives for a Senate intelligence committee confirmation hearing in Washington on 15 July 2026.

sources.originalTitle: US senators urge White House AI chief to fix vulnerabilities after mass outages

segments.body: US senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds have asked Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence and White House AI czar, to identify and fix vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure. Their letter argues that AI can help find weaknesses and accelerate attacks faster than organisations can test and install patches.

segments.title: No established link between the outages
segments.body: The letter follows recent disruptions affecting banks, workplace systems and federal infrastructure. US officials have described failures during software updates and the strain of patching legacy systems; Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said there is no evidence the incidents are connected or the work of one attacker. The senators also want cybersecurity teams to secure the AI systems used to find vulnerabilities.

content.headline: Scotland data-centre proposal draws more than 10,000 representations
content.shortHeadline: Chapelcross data-centre plan draws record public response
content.standfirst: A proposed £16.5bn data centre at the former Chapelcross nuclear site has prompted more submissions to Dumfries and Galloway Council than any other planning application. Concerns include energy bills and grid capacity; the council has yet to publish its assessment.

image.caption: Plans for a data centre at the former Chapelcross nuclear site have drawn thousands of representations.

sources.originalTitle: Council gets most representations ever over data centre

segments.body: Dumfries and Galloway Council has received more than 10,000 representations on plans for a data centre at the former Chapelcross nuclear site near Annan. The proposal, lodged in September, is valued at £16.5bn. A final consultation window closes on 29 November, after which planning officers will process and verify the submissions.

segments.title: Jobs and local costs in dispute
segments.body: Developers say the project could support up to 750 construction jobs and about 540 once operational. Opponents have raised concerns about household bills, pressure on the energy grid and the scale of industrial development, and have challenged the job claims. The council says it will publish a summary of the representations before any decision; their balance of support and objection is not yet clear.

content.headline: Nvidia details conditions on guarantees for AI data-centre loans
content.shortHeadline: Nvidia sets out when its data-centre loan guarantees apply
content.standfirst: Nvidia says its loan guarantees take effect only after customers secure financing and build facilities equipped with its products. The company says this clarifies existing terms, while its interim chief signals a more selective approach to future investment.

sources.originalTitle: Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won’t —keep financing neoclouds
Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

segments.body: Nvidia interim chief executive Colette Kress says the company’s loan guarantees for data-centre projects apply only once customers have secured financing, built the facility and installed Nvidia equipment. If those conditions are not met, the guarantee does not take effect. Kress said the explanation describes existing terms rather than a change in policy.

segments.title: A wider portfolio under review
segments.body: Nvidia reported that its stakes in private companies were worth $65.5bn, up from $22bn in January, and said it invested $16bn in equities in the latest quarter. TechCrunch reports that investors expect Kress to be more selective and write smaller checks; the company says it will rigorously assess future investments and guarantees as the market matures.

perspectives.body: TechCrunch reports that venture investors are bracing for a possible pullback in Nvidia funding, as Kress weighs returning excess cash to shareholders against continued support for the AI ecosystem.

content.headline: A pause in frontier AI training may not slow demand for chips
content.shortHeadline: AI chip demand could outlast a frontier-training slowdown
content.standfirst: Nvidia and AMD report strong sales as the industry’s spending shifts beyond training its largest models. Analysts cited by The Verge say running existing systems could require even more computing capacity, though cheaper custom chips may reshape who benefits.

sources.originalTitle: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either

segments.body: Nvidia’s data-centre revenue rose 110% year on year to $107.6bn in its latest quarter, while AMD’s data-centre sales nearly doubled to $8.5bn, according to The Verge. The reporting argues that even if AI labs slow their biggest training runs, demand could keep growing as companies use existing models more often, including through AI agents.

segments.title: The spending may shift, not disappear
segments.body: Counterpoint Research’s Neil Shah told The Verge that inference—the process of running trained models—could require more computing infrastructure overall than training. The article also notes that falling token prices may encourage use, while companies are developing custom chips to serve models more cheaply. The balance between GPU demand and custom processors remains unsettled.

content.headline: Humyn Labs raises $47m to collect data for robotics and physical AI
content.shortHeadline: Humyn Labs raises $47m for real-world robot training data
content.standfirst: The Indian startup records people doing everyday tasks and turns the footage into training data for robotics companies. Its growth highlights the demand for physical-world data as well as questions about consent and recording inside homes.

sources.originalTitle: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need

segments.body: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47m in equity and venture debt to collect and label footage of people performing everyday tasks for robotics and AI companies. The startup says it uses two-camera hardware and gathers data in more than 20 countries, with Brazil, India and South Korea as main hubs.

segments.title: The consent question
segments.body: The company says it has 12 paying customers and that about 90% of its revenue comes from the US. Its founders say workers record their usual jobs or household chores rather than staged activities, with local partners overseeing collection. The reporting notes wider concerns about privacy and consent when people are filmed in their homes; the company’s account does not resolve those questions.

content.headline: Police and crime commissioner warns of AI voice-cloning scams
content.shortHeadline: Surrey commissioner warns scammers can clone voices with AI
content.standfirst: Surrey’s police and crime commissioner says fraudsters are using AI-generated voices to impersonate people. She claims just three seconds of a victim’s voice can be enough, amid UK figures showing £1.3bn stolen in reported fraud in 2025.

image.caption: Surrey Police and Crime Commissioner Lisa Townsend has warned about voice-cloning scams.

source.credit: Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Surrey

sources.originalTitle: Scammers are exploiting AI technology, PCC warns

segments.body: Surrey Police and Crime Commissioner Lisa Townsend has warned that AI voice-cloning scams have become common in recent months. She demonstrated the technology using a replica of her own voice and said criminals can use a short recording to generate sentences in someone’s likeness.

segments.title: A broader fraud problem
segments.body: Townsend says three seconds of a person’s voice may be enough to clone it. UK Finance figures cited by the BBC show £1.3bn was stolen by scammers in 2025, across more than four million reported fraud cases involving money. The report includes warnings from Surrey residents about increasingly sophisticated scams, but does not provide an independent test of the three-second claim.

content.headline: Cricket Australia opens confidential forum on 2018 sandpapergate scandal
content.shortHeadline: Cricket Australia opens forum on sandpapergate
content.standfirst: The independent forum is intended to let players and staff share their accounts of the ball-tampering scandal. It comes as fresh claims about who knew of the plan have reopened divisions in Australian cricket.

sources.originalTitle: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences

segments.body: Cricket Australia has launched a confidential, independent forum for players and staff involved in the 2018 sandpapergate scandal to give their accounts. Chief executive Todd Greenberg says it is not a new investigation, nobody will be forced to take part and no further penalties will be imposed.

segments.title: Disputed accounts
segments.body: Usman Khawaja’s recent memoir says the whole team knew about the plan to tamper with the ball. The original investigation found three players knew; Khawaja, David Warner and Chadd Sayers have since said they believed everyone knew. Pat Cummins has rejected claims that he knew sandpaper was being taken onto the field.

Greenberg says some players were not heard in the original inquiry and that the forum offers an opportunity to speak without judgement or sanction. The board will decide what, if anything, becomes public. Greenberg also acknowledged that Cricket Australia played a role in the win-at-all-costs culture of the time.

content.headline: Northern Ireland earn historic Nations League A promotion with Hungary draw
content.shortHeadline: Northern Ireland secure historic Nations League promotion
content.standfirst: Justin Devenny’s equaliser earned a 1-1 draw in Budapest and sent Northern Ireland into League A for the first time. Michael O’Neill praised the response after his side went behind for the first time in the campaign.

image.caption: Northern Ireland celebrate securing promotion to Nations League A.

sources.originalTitle: Belief and bench help NI scale new heights

segments.body: Northern Ireland secured promotion to Nations League A for the first time with a 1-1 draw against Hungary. Barnabas Varga put the hosts ahead after 35 minutes, but Justin Devenny’s equaliser earned the point Michael O’Neill’s side needed to top Group B2.

segments.title: Belief and depth
segments.body: O’Neill said his side showed belief in a difficult stadium after falling behind for the first time in the campaign. He made a half-time change and brought on Josh Magennis, with Kieran Morrison and Paul Smyth also entering later; the manager said the fresh legs helped turn the game.

Northern Ireland conceded only once in six games and finished the campaign with 12 points, despite injuries to Conor Bradley, Ali McCann and Daniel Ballard and Jamie Donley’s suspension for the finale. O’Neill says returning players and emerging options should strengthen competition for places before the side steps up to League A.

content.headline: Rassie Erasmus handed six-match ban over comments on match officials
content.shortHeadline: Erasmus receives six-match ban over officials comments
content.standfirst: World Rugby’s independent panel found the South Africa coach’s remarks crossed the threshold for serious misconduct. South Africa Rugby has requested a full hearing, so the suspension’s status remains unresolved.

image.caption: Rassie Erasmus speaking at a news conference in Dublin.

sources.originalTitle: South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches

segments.body: Rassie Erasmus has been given a six-match suspension over remarks questioning the officiating in South Africa’s 21-19 defeat by France. World Rugby says the panel concluded that his comments suggested officials had acted with bias or deliberately influenced the match.

segments.title: Hearing requested
segments.body: Erasmus questioned whether missed hip-drop and knee-drop tackles and non-intervention by the television match official amounted to manipulation. He said he was not making an accusation. South Africa Rugby has asked for a full misconduct hearing so he can put his comments in context and address their intent.

World Rugby says the suspension bars Erasmus from match-day involvement, including coaching, contact with players or management, and entering the stadium or technical areas. If upheld, he would miss Saturday’s Ireland game, next week’s finals weekend fixture and the start of South Africa’s Rugby Championship campaign next summer.

content.headline: Tiger Woods named in Hero World Challenge field for expected December return
content.shortHeadline: Woods set for December return at Hero World Challenge
content.standfirst: The 15-time major champion is in the 20-player field for the Bahamas event, which he hosts. It would be his first competitive appearance in more than two years, after a prolonged absence amid injuries and personal difficulties.

image.caption: Tiger Woods, a 15-time major champion.

sources.originalTitle: Woods set to return next month after two years out

segments.body: Tiger Woods has been named in the field for December’s Hero World Challenge, the tournament he hosts in the Bahamas. He has not played in a traditional ranking event since the 2024 Open Championship and said he has been training and feeling better.

segments.title: A long absence
segments.body: Woods, 50, has dealt with multiple back operations, serious leg injuries from a 2021 car crash and a ruptured Achilles tendon in 2025. He also stepped away from golf to seek treatment after accepting a five-year driving ban following a plea agreement in a reckless-driving case.

content.headline: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf winds down
content.shortHeadline: DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV collapse
content.standfirst: The two-time US Open champion has agreed to play on the European-based tour next season, joining a group of former LIV players returning to its events. His membership gives him access to the full schedule.

image.caption: Bryson DeChambeau, who joined LIV Golf in 2022.

sources.originalTitle: DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf collapse

segments.body: Bryson DeChambeau has secured DP World Tour membership for next season after LIV Golf confirmed it intends to wind down. As a recent major champion, he has category-one membership, guaranteeing entry to events across the season. He has also confirmed he will play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in December.

segments.title: A changing tour landscape
segments.body: Former LIV players Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson are among those invited to a limited number of events, while Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are returning as full-time members. The DP World Tour says its approach aims to add value to tournaments while protecting playing opportunities for its existing members.

A top-10 finish on the DP World Tour’s season standings can secure a PGA Tour card for the following year, offering a possible route back to that circuit. The report notes that Patrick Reed used the pathway after leaving LIV before the 2026 season.

content.headline: Troy Parrott scores twice as Republic of Ireland beat Kosovo 3-0
content.shortHeadline: Parrott double puts Ireland in Nations League play-off
content.standfirst: The win secured Ireland second place in their Nations League group and a place in a March play-off for promotion. Parrott’s two penalties took his international tally to 17, with 12 goals in his past nine competitive appearances.

image.caption: Troy Parrott, who has scored 17 goals for the Republic of Ireland.

sources.originalTitle: Talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals

segments.body: Troy Parrott scored two penalties as the Republic of Ireland beat Kosovo 3-0 to finish second in Nations League Group B3. The result puts them in a two-legged play-off against a League A side in March, with promotion to the top tier at stake.

segments.title: A breakthrough year
segments.body: The goals took Parrott to 17 in 43 international appearances; 12 have come in his past nine competitive matches. After starring for AZ Alkmaar, he joined Real Betis in the summer and has also scored against Real Madrid and in the Champions League.

Ireland’s second-place finish also puts them in pot two for next month’s Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Parrott said the team had been determined to avoid another near miss, while acknowledging that qualification for the tournament is not guaranteed.

content.headline: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton to reach ATP Finals semi-finals
content.shortHeadline: Zverev beats Shelton to reach ATP Finals last four
content.standfirst: A 6-2 7-6 win over Shelton sends the world number one through with a group match to spare. Arthur Fils also stayed in contention after beating Rafael Jodar in three sets.

image.caption: Alexander Zverev, who has won 67 matches this season.

sources.originalTitle: Ruthless Zverev through to ATP Finals knockout stage

segments.body: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-2 7-6 (7-4) to secure a place in the ATP Finals semi-finals with a match to spare. The two-time champion made 25 winners and just 10 unforced errors, and lost only two of the 31 points played on his serve in the second set.

segments.title: Group still in play
segments.body: Arthur Fils recovered from losing the first set to beat Rafael Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2, keeping his hopes of a semi-final place alive. He will face the already-qualified Zverev in the final group match; Shelton is also still part of the group-stage picture.

content.headline: Seb Atkinson set for England return against New Zealand
content.shortHeadline: Atkinson poised for England return against All Blacks
content.standfirst: The centre has recovered from a hip knock and is expected to start against New Zealand at Twickenham. England say they are preparing for the strongest opposition regardless of the All Blacks’ shock defeat by Wales.

image.caption: England centre Seb Atkinson, who has won eight caps.

sources.originalTitle: England's Atkinson set for All Blacks dream date

segments.body: Seb Atkinson is set to return to England’s starting side at number 12 for Saturday’s match against New Zealand at Twickenham. The Gloucester centre has recovered from a hip knock and called the meeting a childhood dream.

segments.title: A major test
segments.body: Atkinson could face Jordie Barrett in midfield. New Zealand are looking to respond after their first defeat by Wales in 73 years, but England senior coach Richard Wigglesworth said that result changes nothing about the challenge his side expect.
